strings.name: Yuna Kim
strings.role: Figure skater and UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador
strings.summary: Yuna Kim became a defining Korean women’s singles skater through jump quality, speed and musical expression, winning Olympic gold and silver and two world titles. Her success broadened skating’s audience in Korea. After ending competition in 2014, she continued advocacy and philanthropy. A UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador since 2010, she donated signed children’s skates in 2026 for a planned children’s-aid auction.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 16, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: An Olympic champion who increased international attention to Korean figure skating and winter sport.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.highlights.h1.title: Olympic and world titles
strings.highlights.h1.text: Won Vancouver Olympic gold in 2010, Sochi silver in 2014 and world championships in 2009 and 2013.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Started skating at six, grew up and trained in Gunpo and later studied physical education at Korea University.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Advocating for children
strings.highlights.h2.text: As UNICEF ambassador, supported children affected by disasters and conflict and programmes promoting sporting participation.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Donated signed children’s skates
strings.timeline.t1.text: A report confirmed her donation for UNICEF’s anniversary auction, scheduled for November 20 and still future at the November 16 cutoff.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Lit the PyeongChang cauldron
strings.timeline.t2.text: Lit the Olympic flame at the opening ceremony in South Korea as a retired Olympic champion.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Olympic silver and competitive retirement
strings.timeline.t3.text: Won women’s singles silver in Sochi and ended her competitive career afterward.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Second world title
strings.timeline.t4.text: Returned to major competition and won her second world championship in London, Canada.
strings.timeline.t5.title: UNICEF appointment
strings.timeline.t5.text: Became an international Goodwill Ambassador, using her sporting platform for children’s relief and rights.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Vancouver Olympic champion
strings.timeline.t6.text: Won with 228.56 points, becoming the first Korean Olympic figure-skating medallist.
strings.timeline.t7.title: First senior world title
strings.timeline.t7.text: Won in Los Angeles, becoming Korea’s first world champion in the discipline.
strings.timeline.t8.title: World Junior champion
strings.timeline.t8.text: Won the women’s junior world title before moving to senior competition.
